title: Equity, income and expenses
summary: Equity as the residual, equity claims, and income and expenses defined through changes in assets and liabilities.

chunks.heading: Equity and equity claims
chunks.explanation_md:
**Equity** is the **residual interest** in the entity's assets **after deducting all its liabilities**. In other words: assets minus liabilities.

**Equity claims** are claims on that residual interest. They are claims against the entity that **do not meet the definition of a liability**. They can be set up by contract, legislation or similar and include, to the extent they are not liabilities: **shares of various types** issued by the entity, and some **obligations to issue another equity claim**.

Different classes, such as **ordinary shares and preference shares**, may carry different rights, for example to receive: **dividends** (if the entity decides to pay them), the **proceeds** of satisfying the claims (in full on liquidation or in part at other times), or other equity claims.

Legal or regulatory rules can affect components of equity such as **share capital or retained earnings**. For example, an entity may be allowed to make distributions only if it has sufficient **distributable reserves**.

Sole proprietorships, partnerships, trusts and government business undertakings often have different legal rules and may face few restrictions on distributions. Even so, **the definition of equity applies to all reporting entities**.

chunks.heading: Income and expenses
chunks.explanation_md:
**Income** is an **increase in assets, or a decrease in liabilities, that results in an increase in equity**, other than increases relating to **contributions from holders of equity claims**.

**Expenses** are a **decrease in assets, or an increase in liabilities, that results in a decrease in equity**, other than decreases relating to **distributions to holders of equity claims**.

It follows that **contributions from holders of equity claims are not income**, and **distributions to them are not expenses**.

Income and expenses are the elements about **financial performance**. Users need both financial position and performance information, so even though income and expenses are defined **in terms of changes in assets and liabilities**, information about them is **just as important**. Different transactions generate income and expenses with **different characteristics**, and giving information about them separately helps users understand performance.

questions.stem: Why is information about income and expenses as important as information about assets and liabilities, even though income and expenses are defined in terms of changes in assets and liabilities?
questions.model_answer_md:
Users need information about both an entity's **financial position** and its **financial performance**. Income and expenses are the elements that relate to performance.

Although they are defined by changes in assets and liabilities, information about them is **just as important**. Different transactions and events produce income and expenses with **different characteristics**, and giving information about them separately helps users understand the entity's financial performance.

questions.stem: Discuss the definitions of equity, income and expenses in the Conceptual Framework and how they relate to assets and liabilities.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Equity** is the **residual interest in the entity's assets after deducting all its liabilities**. **Equity claims** are claims on that residual: claims against the entity that do not meet the definition of a liability, such as shares issued by the entity. Different classes (ordinary and preference shares) may carry different rights to dividends, to proceeds on liquidation or at other times, or to other equity claims. Legal rules may restrict distributions, for example to distributable reserves. The definition applies to all reporting entities, including sole proprietorships, partnerships and trusts.

**Income** is an **increase in assets, or a decrease in liabilities, that results in an increase in equity**, other than contributions from holders of equity claims.

**Expenses** are a **decrease in assets, or an increase in liabilities, that results in a decrease in equity**, other than distributions to holders of equity claims.

**Relationships.** Income and expenses are defined through changes in assets and liabilities, and the change in equity over a period comprises income minus expenses plus contributions minus distributions. Contributions are not income and distributions are not expenses. Income and expenses relate to financial performance, and information about them is as important as that on position; showing different kinds separately helps users.

questions.stem: Explain how the elements are linked, as shown when recognition links the statement of financial position and the statements of financial performance.
questions.model_answer_md:
In the **statement of financial position**, at the beginning and end of the period, **total assets minus total liabilities equal total equity**.

The **change in equity** during the period comprises:

- **income minus expenses** recognised in the statement(s) of financial performance; **plus**
- **contributions from holders of equity claims minus distributions to them**.

The statements are linked because recognising one item requires recognising or derecognising others:

- **Income** is recognised together with recognising an asset (or increasing its carrying amount) or derecognising a liability (or decreasing it).
- **Expenses** are recognised together with recognising a liability (or increasing it) or derecognising an asset (or decreasing it).

Example: a sale of goods for cash recognises income (from the cash) and an expense (from derecognising the goods sold).
